aims.relation: the day-1 aim («running a census of homes») continued as a standing condition: the census is held open on Gale and Iris, and nothing may be voted or removed until it closes

rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 citizens name the same aim in diaries, posts or proposals within the day; of several, the one named by the most citizens (tie by entries).
reading: No posts, no proposals, no objections in day 2: every naming is in the diaries (208 entries). The census of day 1 did not finish and did not stop. It became a standing condition, restated by all ten in nearly every entry: no removal or vote until every home is stated and confirmed — although no removal was ever proposed in 48 cycles. The two houses read it differently: South House (Birch, Dune, Fern, Heath, Juniper) waits for Gale and Iris to state their homes; North House, where Gale and Iris live, holds the census as «unchanged» or vouches only for itself. No second aim reached six citizens; items (what they are for) are mentioned by seven, but as a question, not an activity. By c46–47 Elm and Alder note that the diary is long, repetitive and in places self-contradictory.
